metadata.purpose: Seed evidence pack for the UniMelb Open Day 2026 multi-agent debate demo
metadata.warning: Review every source shortly before the event. Exclude volatile admissions, fees, rankings, employment and salary claims from P0.

facts.claim: The Computing and Software Systems major is available through both the Bachelor of Science and the Bachelor of Design.
facts.sourceTitle: Computing and Software Systems - The University of Melbourne

facts.claim: The major develops practical skills in programming, analysing computer networks and software development processes.
facts.sourceTitle: Computing and Software Systems - The University of Melbourne

facts.claim: Bachelor of Science students can study computer science subjects from first year, complete foundational mathematics and computing, and take four advanced Computing and Software Systems subjects in third year.
facts.sourceTitle: Computing and Software Systems Major Structure

facts.claim: The Bachelor of Science offers more than 40 majors across science, biomedicine, mathematics, engineering and IT subjects.
facts.sourceTitle: Bachelor of Science - The University of Melbourne

facts.claim: UniMelb's IT and computer science study area highlights AI, cybersecurity, internships and industry projects.
facts.sourceTitle: Information Technology and Computer Science | Study at Melbourne

facts.claim: The Parkville campus is the University's historic main campus and combines heritage buildings around the Old Quadrangle with contemporary architecture, within walking distance of central Melbourne.
facts.sourceTitle: Open Day at the University of Melbourne
facts.notes: Beauty remains subjective; use this as descriptive evidence only.

facts.claim: The University states that students can explore more than 200 clubs and societies at Melbourne.
facts.sourceTitle: Open Day at the University of Melbourne

facts.claim: Monash offers a dedicated Bachelor of Information Technology at Clayton with a three-year full-time duration.
The Bachelor of Information Technology is described as flexible, with a broad range of majors, minors and electives.
Listed areas include artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, computer science, software development, games and immersive media, data science and business AI systems.
The course page describes professional placement units and other work-integrated learning opportunities such as placements.
Monash describes student-run clubs, societies and groups across interests including social, cultural, academic, political, sporting and performing activities.
facts.sourceTitle: Clubs, societies and groups - Monash University
